notes: Held-out set written blind: its author did not open src/ or any file under bench/memory/ (no ranking code, no first dataset, no results) and wrote every entry and request from the schema and the task brief alone, without tuning wording to any tokenizer or keyword list. Three projects in domains the brief left open (a Go gRPC CLI and daemon on SQLite, a Django/DRF/Celery/Redis clinic scheduler on Fly.io, an Expo React Native driver app on Supabase), each with the owner's own rules (in Spanish and English, never gold), two superseded pairs, failures quoting exact error text, entries with related files, and look-alike entries across projects (migrations, environment variables, releases, flaky tests, lint). Requests are typed the way the owner writes: about half Spanish, English code terms mixed in, short follow-ups that only make sense with the previous request, vague complaints, slang and a few typos; paraphrases deliberately avoid the entries' vocabulary. Gold lists what must reach the model, acceptable what may, forbidden the superseded facts and other projects' look-alikes that must not be presented as current; irrelevant requests have empty gold.

projects.description: Go 1.23 CLI (spctl) and gRPC daemon (stockpiled) tracking warehouse inventory in SQLite; protos with buf, releases with goreleaser.

entries.title: Sin cgo en el binario
entries.hook: Regla del dueño sobre cómo se compila el binario
entries.description: El binario de release se compila siempre con CGO_ENABLED=0; nada de dependencias que requieran cgo.
entries.body: Nada de cgo en el binario. Se compila con `CGO_ENABLED=0` siempre y se distribuye estático. Si una librería pide cgo, se busca otra.

entries.title: Wrap errors, never log-and-return
entries.hook: Owner rule on error handling
entries.description: Always wrap errors with %w and a lowercase context; never log an error and also return it.
entries.body: Always wrap errors with context, `fmt.Errorf("load config: %w", err)` style: lowercase, no trailing punctuation. Never log an error and return it too; whoever handles it logs it.

entries.title: Published protos only grow
entries.hook: Owner rule on changing the public API
entries.description: Fields in stockpile.v1 are only added, never renumbered or removed; breaking changes go to a v2 package.
entries.body: stockpile.v1 is published: only add fields. Never renumber, rename or delete a field; mark it `reserved` instead. A breaking change means a new `stockpile.v2` package.

entries.title: Tests en tabla, sin testify/suite
entries.hook: Regla del dueño sobre el estilo de los tests
entries.description: Los tests son table-driven con t.Run; no se usa testify/suite ni mocks generados.
entries.body: Tests table-driven con `t.Run(tc.name, ...)`, un caso por fila. Nada de testify/suite ni mocks generados; fakes escritos a mano en `internal/fakes`.

entries.title: spctl → gRPC → stockpiled → store
entries.hook: How the CLI, the daemon and the SQLite store fit together
entries.description: The spctl CLI dials the stockpiled daemon over gRPC; only internal/store touches SQL.
entries.body:
- `cmd/spctl` (cobra) is a thin gRPC client; it never opens the database.
- `cmd/stockpiled` serves `stockpile.v1.StockService`, implemented in `internal/server/stock_service.go`.
- Default listen address: `unix:///run/stockpile/stockpiled.sock` on Linux, `127.0.0.1:7431` on Windows.
- All SQL lives in `internal/store`; the server calls store methods, never `database/sql` directly.

entries.title: Regenerate protos with make proto
entries.hook: How to regenerate Go code from the .proto files
entries.description: make proto runs protoc with protoc-gen-go and protoc-gen-go-grpc into pkg/pb.
entries.body:
Run `make proto`. It calls `protoc --go_out=pkg/pb --go-grpc_out=pkg/pb -I proto proto/stockpile/v1/*.proto`.
Needs protoc 3.21 plus `protoc-gen-go` and `protoc-gen-go-grpc` on PATH.

entries.title: Protos are generated with buf
entries.hook: Regenerating gRPC code and the buf checks CI runs
entries.description: buf generate writes gen/go/stockpile/v1; CI runs buf lint and buf breaking against main.
entries.body:
- Regenerate: `buf generate` from the repo root (config in `buf.gen.yaml`, remote plugins, no local protoc needed).
- Output goes to `gen/go/stockpile/v1`; never edit generated files, they are overwritten.
- CI runs `buf lint` and `buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main'`; a removed or renumbered field fails there.
- `make proto` was removed in the move to buf.

entries.title: SQLite through mattn/go-sqlite3
entries.hook: Which SQLite driver the store uses and what building it needs
entries.description: The store uses github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3, so builds need CGO_ENABLED=1 and a C compiler.
entries.body:
Driver is `github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3` (`sql.Open("sqlite3", path)`).
Builds need `CGO_ENABLED=1` and gcc; on Windows install TDM-GCC or MSYS2 mingw-w64 and put it on PATH.

entries.title: Pure-Go SQLite: modernc.org/sqlite
entries.hook: Why the store uses modernc.org/sqlite and how to open it
entries.description: Moved from mattn/go-sqlite3 to modernc.org/sqlite so releases build with CGO_ENABLED=0 and need no C compiler.
entries.body:
- Driver: `modernc.org/sqlite`, registered as `"sqlite"` (not `"sqlite3"`).
- DSN: `file:/var/lib/stockpile/stockpile.db?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)`.
- No gcc needed on any OS; goreleaser cross-compiles every target.
- Rejected: keeping mattn and cross-compiling with `zig cc` (broke twice in goreleaser on darwin/arm64).

entries.title: database is locked (SQLITE_BUSY) under concurrent writes
entries.hook: SQLITE_BUSY errors when several RPCs write at the same time
entries.description: Concurrent writes failed with SQLITE_BUSY until writes went through a single-connection pool with busy_timeout.
entries.body:
Error: `database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)` when two `spctl count` runs hit RecordCount together.
Fix in `internal/store/store.go`:
- write pool: `writeDB.SetMaxOpenConns(1)`; a separate read pool opened with `?mode=ro`.
- keep `_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)` in the DSN; WAL mode is what lets readers run during a write.
- start write transactions with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (`store.WithTx` does it) to avoid lock-upgrade deadlocks.

entries.title: sql: unknown driver "sqlite3" after the driver swap
entries.hook: The daemon cannot open the database right after changing the SQLite driver
entries.description: After moving to modernc, code still opening "sqlite3" fails at startup; use the driver name "sqlite" and the blank import.
entries.body:
Error at startup: `sql: unknown driver "sqlite3" (forgotten import?)`.
- modernc registers the name `"sqlite"`: `sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)`.
- The blank import `_ "modernc.org/sqlite"` lives in `internal/store/open.go`; tools that open the DB themselves (`cmd/spmigrate`) need it too.
- `grep -rn '"sqlite3"' --include=*.go .` finds leftovers.

entries.title: spctl: Unavailable, dial unix ... no such file or directory
entries.hook: spctl cannot reach the daemon
entries.description: Unavailable with no such file means the daemon is not running or listens somewhere other than where spctl dials.
entries.body:
Error: `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial unix /run/stockpile/stockpiled.sock: connect: no such file or directory"`.
1. `systemctl status stockpiled` and `journalctl -u stockpiled -n 50`.
2. spctl dials `$STOCKPILE_ADDR` or `--addr`; it must match the daemon's `--listen`.
3. `/run` is tmpfs: the unit needs `RuntimeDirectory=stockpile`, or the socket directory is gone after a reboot.

entries.title: spctl import: DeadlineExceeded on large CSV files
entries.hook: Imports of big CSV files time out
entries.description: The unary ImportItems call hits the 10s client deadline on large files; use the streaming RPC or a longer --timeout.
entries.body:
Error: `rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded` on `spctl import items.csv` (~80k rows).
- spctl's default per-call timeout is 10s (`--timeout`).
- Proper fix: `spctl import --stream` uses the client-streaming `ImportItemsStream` RPC, 500 rows per message, one transaction per batch.
- Quick workaround: `spctl import --timeout 3m items.csv`.

entries.title: ResourceExhausted: received message larger than max
entries.hook: Listing all items fails once the catalog is large
entries.description: ListItems responses passed gRPC's 4 MiB default; paginate with page tokens instead of raising the limit.
entries.body:
Error: `rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (5242880 vs. 4194304)`.
- Don't raise `MaxCallRecvMsgSize`; `ListItems` takes `page_size` (max 1000) and returns `next_page_token`.
- `spctl ls` pages automatically since v0.7; scripts calling the API must loop on `next_page_token`.

entries.title: Running the Go tests
entries.hook: Commands to run the test suite, with and without the race detector
entries.description: go test -race -count=1 ./... in CI; -race needs cgo, so on Windows without gcc run it without -race.
entries.body:
- Full suite: `go test -race -count=1 ./...` (CI on Linux sets `CGO_ENABLED=1` for tests only).
- `-race` requires cgo; on Windows without gcc run `go test -count=1 ./...` and rely on CI for races.
- Integration tests are behind a build tag and start a real daemon on a temp socket: `go test -tags integration ./internal/server/...`.

entries.title: TestWatchStock_ReceivesUpdates is flaky
entries.hook: A streaming test that fails about once in twenty runs
entries.description: The watch test sleeps 50ms before sending an update and sometimes misses it; wait on the server's subscribed hook instead.
entries.body:
`TestWatchStock_ReceivesUpdates` in `internal/server/watch_test.go` fails ~1 in 20 with `timed out waiting for update`.
Likely cause: `time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)` before the update races the stream subscription.
Fix (not merged yet): wait on the `srv.OnWatchSubscribed` channel instead of sleeping.
Check a fix with `go test -run TestWatchStock -count=50 ./internal/server/`.

entries.title: CLI output is tested with golden files
entries.hook: Updating expected CLI output in tests
entries.description: spctl table and json output is compared against cmd/spctl/testdata/*.golden; regenerate with the -update flag.
entries.body:
- Tests in `cmd/spctl/output_test.go` compare against `cmd/spctl/testdata/<name>.golden`.
- Regenerate after an intended change: `go test ./cmd/spctl/ -run TestOutput -update`, then review `git diff cmd/spctl/testdata`.
- Golden files must stay LF: `core.autocrlf=true` broke them once on Windows; `.gitattributes` has `*.golden -text`.

entries.title: Schema migrations with goose
entries.hook: Adding or changing a table in the SQLite schema
entries.description: Migrations are goose SQL files embedded in the daemon and applied at startup.
entries.body:
- Create: `goose -dir internal/store/migrations create add_bin_location sql`.
- Each file needs `-- +goose Up` and `-- +goose Down` sections; files are embedded with `//go:embed migrations/*.sql`.
- The daemon applies pending migrations on start; `spctl admin migrate-status` shows the current version.
- `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL` needs a `DEFAULT` in SQLite.

entries.title: Releasing spctl and stockpiled
entries.hook: Cutting a tagged release
entries.description: Push a vX.Y.Z tag on main; GitHub Actions runs goreleaser, which builds all targets and updates the Homebrew tap.
entries.body:
1. Update `CHANGELOG.md` and merge to main.
2. `git tag -a v0.9.0 -m "v0.9.0" && git push origin v0.9.0`.
3. `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs `goreleaser release --clean` (needs the `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` secret).
Dry run locally: `goreleaser release --snapshot --clean` (artifacts in `dist/`, nothing published).

entries.title: Config precedence and STOCKPILE_DB
entries.hook: Where stockpiled takes its settings from, and the relative-path trap
entries.description: Flags beat STOCKPILE_* env vars, which beat /etc/stockpile/config.toml; a relative STOCKPILE_DB lands in /.
entries.body:
- Precedence: flags > `STOCKPILE_*` env vars > `/etc/stockpile/config.toml` > defaults (viper).
- `STOCKPILE_DB` must be absolute: under systemd the working dir is `/`, so `STOCKPILE_DB=stockpile.db` silently creates `/stockpile.db` with an empty schema.
- `stockpiled config print` shows every resolved value and where it came from.

entries.title: Adding an spctl subcommand
entries.hook: Where and how new CLI subcommands are written
entries.description: One file per subcommand in cmd/spctl, RunE, output through the shared printer that honours --output.
entries.body:
- One file per command: `cmd/spctl/cmd_<name>.go`, registered in its `init()` with `rootCmd.AddCommand`.
- Use `RunE` and return errors; never `os.Exit` inside a command.
- Print through `printer.New(cmd)` so `--output table|json|yaml` works; add a golden file for the table output.

entries.title: golangci-lint setup
entries.hook: Lint command and the nolint policy
entries.description: golangci-lint with errcheck, gosec and revive; nolint only with a reason comment.
entries.body:
- `golangci-lint run ./...` (config `.golangci.yml`: errcheck, gosec, revive, gofumpt, nolintlint).
- Suppress only with a reason: `//nolint:gosec // path comes from an admin-only flag`; a bare `//nolint` fails `nolintlint`.
- `gofumpt -l -w .` fixes the formatting findings.

entries.title: All quantity changes go through store.AdjustStock
entries.hook: Changing an item's quantity without losing the movement history
entries.description: AdjustStock writes the stock_movements row and updates items.qty in one transaction.
entries.body:
- `store.AdjustStock(ctx, tx, sku, delta, reason)` inserts into `stock_movements` and updates `items.qty` in the same transaction.
- Call it inside `store.WithTx(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { ... })`.
- Never `UPDATE items SET qty = ...` directly: the nightly `spctl admin reconcile` flags any item whose qty differs from the sum of its movements.

entries.title: No TLS on the local gRPC socket
entries.hook: How access to the daemon is controlled
entries.description: Access is controlled by the socket's file mode and group; mTLS was considered and rejected.
entries.body:
- On Linux the daemon listens only on a unix socket (mode `0660`, group `stockpile`); users in that group can run spctl.
- Rejected: mTLS with per-device certificates (rotating certs on 40 warehouse boxes without MDM was not manageable).
- Remote access, if ever needed, goes through `ssh -L`, not a TCP listener.

entries.title: Windows: unix socket listen fails
entries.hook: stockpiled does not start on Windows with a unix: listen address
entries.description: Windows builds default to TCP 127.0.0.1:7431; forcing a unix: address fails on some Windows builds and VMs.
entries.body:
Error: `listen unix C:\ProgramData\stockpile\stockpiled.sock: bind: An address incompatible with the requested protocol was used.`
- The Windows default is `--listen 127.0.0.1:7431`; don't pass `unix:` there.
- spctl on Windows needs `STOCKPILE_ADDR=127.0.0.1:7431` if an old config still names the socket.

entries.title: Backing up the live database
entries.hook: Taking a consistent copy of the database while the daemon runs
entries.description: Use spctl admin backup (VACUUM INTO); copying the .db file alone misses the WAL.
entries.body:
- `spctl admin backup --out /var/backups/stockpile-$(date +%F).db` runs `VACUUM INTO` in the daemon; consistent while it serves.
- Never `cp stockpile.db` while it runs: recent writes live in `stockpile.db-wal`, so the copy is stale or corrupt.
- Restore: stop the service, replace the file, delete the `-wal` and `-shm` files, start it.

projects.description: Django 5 + DRF + Celery + Redis backend for a physiotherapy clinic network's appointment scheduling and SMS reminders (Postgres, Twilio), deployed on Fly.io.

entries.title: No ORM calls in views
entries.hook: Owner rule on where queries live
entries.description: Views and serializers never query the ORM directly; reads go through selectors, writes through services.
entries.body: Views and serializers never call the ORM directly. Reads go through `<app>/selectors.py`, writes through `<app>/services.py`. A view that does `Appointment.objects...` doesn't get merged.

entries.title: Fechas en UTC, zona de la clínica solo al mostrar
entries.hook: Regla del dueño sobre fechas y zonas horarias
entries.description: Todo se guarda en UTC; la conversión a la zona de cada clínica se hace solo al presentar.
entries.body: Todas las fechas se guardan en UTC. La zona de la clínica (`clinic.tz`) se aplica solo al mostrar o al interpretar lo que escribe el usuario. Prohibido `datetime.now()` pelado: siempre `timezone.now()`.

entries.title: Cero datos reales de pacientes fuera de producción
entries.hook: Regla del dueño sobre privacidad
entries.description: No copiar datos reales de pacientes a fixtures, logs, issues ni al chat.
entries.body: Jamás pegues datos reales de pacientes (nombres, teléfonos, diagnósticos) en fixtures, logs, issues ni en el chat. Para pruebas, `PatientFactory`. Si ves un log con el teléfono completo, se enmascara.

entries.title: Celery tasks are idempotent and take IDs
entries.hook: Owner rule for background tasks
entries.description: Every task can run twice safely and receives primary keys, never model instances.
entries.body: Every Celery task must be safe to run twice and take primary keys (`appointment_id`), never model instances or querysets. Retries are expected, not exceptional.

entries.title: Django apps and layering
entries.hook: What lives where in the backend
entries.description: Apps scheduling, patients, notifications, billing and core; logic in services and selectors; settings split by environment.
entries.body:
- `scheduling/` (Clinic, Practitioner, Slot, Appointment), `patients/`, `notifications/` (SMS via Twilio), `billing/`, `core/` (auth, permissions, exceptions).
- Writes in `<app>/services.py`, reads in `<app>/selectors.py`, DRF viewsets in `<app>/views.py` under `/api/v1/`.
- Settings: `config/settings/{base,dev,test,prod}.py`; the Celery app is in `config/celery.py`.

entries.title: Running Celery locally
entries.hook: Starting the worker and beat in development
entries.description: Celery app in config/celery.py with Redis db 0 as broker; worker and beat run as separate processes.
entries.body:
- Broker `REDIS_URL` (db 0), results in db 1; the app in `config/celery.py` calls `app.autodiscover_tasks()`.
- Worker: `celery -A config worker -l info -Q default,sms`.
- Beat: `celery -A config beat -l info --scheduler django_celery_beat.schedulers:DatabaseScheduler`.
- Periodic tasks are declared in `CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE` in `config/settings/base.py`.
- `settings.dev` does not run tasks eagerly: start Redis first with `docker compose up -d redis`.

entries.title: Deploying to Heroku
entries.hook: How the backend is deployed to production
entries.description: git push heroku main; the release phase runs migrate and a worker dyno runs Celery.
entries.body:
- `git push heroku main` deploys; the `Procfile` release phase runs `python manage.py migrate --noinput`.
- Celery runs on dynos: `heroku ps:scale worker=1 beat=1 -a agenda-clinica`.
- Logs: `heroku logs --tail -a agenda-clinica`.

entries.title: Deploying production on Fly.io
entries.hook: How the backend reaches production
entries.description: fly deploy on agenda-clinica-prod; migrations run as the release command; app, worker and beat are Fly processes.
entries.body:
- `fly deploy -a agenda-clinica-prod` (config `fly.toml`, image from `Dockerfile`).
- `[deploy] release_command = "python manage.py migrate --noinput"`; a failing migration aborts the deploy before traffic moves.
- Processes: `app` (gunicorn), `worker` (celery), `beat`; logs with `fly logs -a agenda-clinica-prod`.
- Heroku was shut down in June 2026; the `heroku` git remote is dead.

entries.title: Staging on Fly
entries.hook: Deploying to and using the staging environment
entries.description: agenda-clinica-staging uses fly.staging.toml, a nightly anonymized database and Twilio test credentials.
entries.body:
- Deploy: `fly deploy -a agenda-clinica-staging --config fly.staging.toml`.
- The database is refreshed nightly from an anonymized dump (`make staging-refresh` runs `scripts/anonymize_dump.sh`).
- Twilio uses test credentials: SMS are accepted but never delivered; read them in the `notifications_smslog` table.

entries.title: Reminders via the send_reminders command
entries.hook: How appointment reminder SMS are sent
entries.description: Heroku Scheduler runs manage.py send_reminders every 10 minutes.
entries.body:
- `python manage.py send_reminders` finds appointments starting in 24h and sends the SMS inline.
- Heroku Scheduler runs it every 10 minutes; a Twilio failure is not retried.

entries.title: Reminders are a Celery beat task
entries.hook: How and when appointment reminders go out
entries.description: notifications.tasks.send_due_reminders runs every 5 minutes on beat and enqueues one SMS task per appointment.
entries.body:
- Beat runs `notifications.tasks.send_due_reminders` every 5 minutes (`CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE`).
- It selects appointments 24h and 2h ahead with no `Reminder.sent_at` and enqueues `send_sms_reminder.delay(appointment_id, kind)` on the `sms` queue.
- Twilio errors retry: `autoretry_for=(TwilioRestException,)`, `retry_backoff=True`, `max_retries=5`.
- The old `send_reminders` management command was deleted.

entries.title: Double booking of a slot
entries.hook: Two patients booked the same slot at the same moment
entries.description: Concurrent bookings raced; the slot row is now locked with select_for_update and the unique violation maps to 409.
entries.body:
Symptom: 500 with `IntegrityError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_active_slot_booking"` on `POST /api/v1/appointments/`.
Fix in `scheduling/services.py::book_appointment`:
- `with transaction.atomic(): slot = Slot.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=slot_id)` before checking availability.
- catch `IntegrityError` and raise `SlotTaken` (HTTP 409, code `slot_taken`).

entries.title: Naive datetime warning turns into test failures
entries.hook: RuntimeWarning about naive datetimes when creating appointments
entries.description: Datetimes built without a zone trigger Django's naive-datetime warning, which pytest treats as an error.
entries.body:
Error: `RuntimeWarning: DateTimeField Appointment.starts_at received a naive datetime (2026-05-04 09:00:00) while time zone support is active.`
- pytest runs with `filterwarnings = ["error::RuntimeWarning"]` in `pyproject.toml`, so the test fails.
- Build datetimes with `timezone.make_aware(dt, ZoneInfo(clinic.tz))`, or require ISO strings with an offset in the serializer.

entries.title: Worker discards an unregistered task
entries.hook: Tasks silently dropped after renaming or moving them
entries.description: After a task rename, queued messages with the old name are discarded; keep the old name for a release or purge the queue.
entries.body:
Worker log: `Received unregistered task of type 'notifications.tasks.send_sms_reminder'. The message has been ignored and discarded.`
- Happens when a task is renamed or moved while messages with the old name are queued, or a worker still runs old code.
- Keep the old name for one release: `@shared_task(name="notifications.tasks.send_sms_reminder")`.
- Or purge: `celery -A config purge -Q sms -f` (drops pending reminders; run `send_due_reminders` again after).

entries.title: Redis connection refused in development
entries.hook: Celery or the cache cannot reach Redis locally
entries.description: Redis is not running locally; start it with docker compose.
entries.body:
Error: `kombu.exceptions.OperationalError: Error 111 connecting to localhost:6379. Connection refused.`
- Start it: `docker compose up -d redis`; check with `docker compose exec redis redis-cli ping`.
- With WSL and Docker Desktop use `REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0` (`localhost` resolved to ::1 once).

entries.title: rediss:// URL needs ssl_cert_reqs
entries.hook: Celery fails to start on Fly with the managed Redis URL
entries.description: The managed Redis gives a rediss:// URL; Celery refuses it without ssl_cert_reqs in the query string.
entries.body:
Error on worker boot: `ValueError: A rediss:// URL must have parameter ssl_cert_reqs and this must be set to CERT_REQUIRED, CERT_OPTIONAL, or CERT_NONE`.
- Set the secret with the parameter: `fly secrets set REDIS_URL='rediss://default:<password>@<host>:6379?ssl_cert_reqs=CERT_REQUIRED' -a agenda-clinica-prod`.
- The cache (`django-redis`) uses the same URL and ignores the parameter.

entries.title: Running the test suite
entries.hook: pytest commands, settings and factories
entries.description: pytest with pytest-django and xdist, reusing the test database; factories in tests/factories.py.
entries.body:
- `pytest -n auto --reuse-db` (settings `config.settings.test`, set in `pyproject.toml`).
- After adding a migration run once with `--create-db`, or tests fail with `column ... does not exist`.
- One test: `pytest scheduling/tests/test_booking.py -k slot_taken -n0`.
- Data via factory_boy in `tests/factories.py` (`AppointmentFactory`, `PatientFactory`).

entries.title: Reminder tests fail in DST change weeks
entries.hook: Tests that break only around daylight saving changes
entries.description: test_reminders freezes a naive local time; around the DST switch the 24h window shifts by an hour.
entries.body:
`notifications/tests/test_reminders.py::test_reminder_24h_before` fails in the week of a DST change (last Sunday of March and October).
Cause: `@freeze_time("2026-03-28 09:00")` is naive and read as UTC while the clinic is `Europe/Madrid`.
Fix: freeze aware instants (`freeze_time("2026-03-28T08:00:00+00:00")`) and build expectations with `ZoneInfo(clinic.tz)`.

entries.title: Celery and on_commit in tests
entries.hook: Tasks and on_commit callbacks that never run in tests
entries.description: Tests run tasks eagerly; on_commit callbacks only fire inside django_capture_on_commit_callbacks.
entries.body:
- `config/settings/test.py` sets `CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER = True` and `CELERY_TASK_EAGER_PROPAGATES = True`.
- Services enqueue with `transaction.on_commit(lambda: task.delay(...))`; inside a test transaction that never fires.
- Use the fixture: `with django_capture_on_commit_callbacks(execute=True): book_appointment(...)`.

entries.title: Django migrations workflow
entries.hook: Creating, reviewing and shipping a schema migration
entries.description: makemigrations per app, review with sqlmigrate, data migrations need reverse_code; production runs them in the Fly release command.
entries.body:
- `python manage.py makemigrations scheduling`, then review the SQL: `python manage.py sqlmigrate scheduling 0042`.
- `RunPython` data migrations must pass `reverse_code` (at least `migrations.RunPython.noop`).
- Index on `scheduling_appointment` (8M rows): `AddIndexConcurrently` in a migration with `atomic = False`.
- Before a deploy: `python manage.py migrate --plan` against staging.

entries.title: Environment variables and the .env file
entries.hook: Settings read from the environment, and the missing secret key error
entries.description: django-environ reads env vars; .env is only read when DJANGO_READ_DOT_ENV_FILE=1; production values are Fly secrets.
entries.body:
- `config/settings/base.py` uses django-environ; `.env` is loaded only if `DJANGO_READ_DOT_ENV_FILE=1`.
- A missing key fails at import: `django.core.exceptions.ImproperlyConfigured: Set the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable`.
- Production and staging: `fly secrets set DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=... -a agenda-clinica-prod`; `fly secrets list` shows names only.
- Every variable is listed in `.env.example`.

entries.title: Lint, format and type checks
entries.hook: ruff, mypy and the pre-commit hooks
entries.description: ruff check and ruff format via pre-commit; mypy with django-stubs on the main apps.
entries.body:
- `ruff check . --fix && ruff format .` (config in `pyproject.toml`, line length 100).
- pre-commit runs both on staged files; `pre-commit run --all-files` fixes everything at once.
- Types: `mypy scheduling patients notifications` (django-stubs, djangorestframework-stubs).

entries.title: DRF API conventions
entries.hook: How endpoints, serializers and errors are shaped
entries.description: ViewSets under /api/v1/, separate read and write serializers, cursor pagination and a single error format.
entries.body:
- Serializers come in pairs: `AppointmentReadSerializer` / `AppointmentWriteSerializer`.
- Lists use `CursorPagination` ordered by `-starts_at`.
- Errors are `{"code": "slot_taken", "detail": "..."}` via `core.exceptions.api_exception_handler`; raise `core.exceptions.ApiError(code, detail, status)`.
- Schema with drf-spectacular: `python manage.py spectacular --file schema.yml`.

entries.title: Roles and permissions
entries.hook: Where access rules for receptionists, practitioners and patients are defined
entries.description: Permission classes live in core/permissions.py; querysets are scoped to the user's clinic in each viewset.
entries.body:
- `core/permissions.py`: `IsPractitioner`, `IsReceptionist`, `IsPatientOwner`, `IsClinicAdmin`.
- `DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES = [IsAuthenticated]`; each viewset adds its own in `get_permissions()`.
- Clinic isolation is in `get_queryset()`: filter by `request.user.membership.clinic_id` (see `scheduling/views.py`). A missing filter leaks other clinics' appointments.

entries.title: Slots are precomputed nightly
entries.hook: Why availability comes from a table instead of being calculated per request
entries.description: A nightly task materializes 60 days of slots; computing availability on each request was rejected for latency.
entries.body:
- `scheduling.tasks.generate_slots` runs at 02:00 clinic time and fills `Slot` rows 60 days ahead from each practitioner's `WorkingHours`.
- Changing working hours calls `regenerate_slots(practitioner_id)` for future unbooked slots.
- Rejected: computing free times on each `GET /api/v1/availability/` (p95 of 1.8s with 30 practitioners).

entries.title: Twilio status webhook returns 403 behind Fly
entries.hook: SMS delivery status callbacks rejected in production
entries.description: Signature validation rebuilt the URL as http behind the proxy; SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER fixed it.
entries.body:
Symptom: every `POST /webhooks/twilio/status/` returns 403 and `SmsLog.status` stays `queued`.
- `RequestValidator` checks `X-Twilio-Signature` against the full URL; behind Fly's proxy Django saw `http://`.
- Fix in `config/settings/prod.py`: `SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER = ("HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO", "https")`.
- When testing through a tunnel, the callback URL must match exactly, trailing slash included.

entries.title: Only one beat process
entries.hook: Every reminder SMS sent twice
entries.description: Two beat machines scheduled every periodic task twice; beat must run as exactly one instance.
entries.body:
Incident 2026-07-14: patients got every reminder twice after `fly scale count 2` scaled all processes, `beat` included.
- Keep one: `fly scale count app=2 worker=2 beat=1 -a agenda-clinica-prod`.
- Second guard: `send_sms_reminder` skips when `Reminder.sent_at` is set (`select_for_update` on the Reminder row).

projects.description: Expo (React Native, SDK 51) app for delivery drivers: routes, proof-of-delivery photos, an offline outbox; Supabase backend (Postgres with RLS, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions).

entries.title: No any in TypeScript
entries.hook: Owner rule on types
entries.description: Never use any; use unknown and narrow, or the generated Supabase types.
entries.body: No `any`, not even in tests. Use `unknown` and narrow, or the generated types in `lib/database.types.ts`. A `// @ts-expect-error` needs a comment saying why.

entries.title: Ningún texto a pelo en pantalla
entries.hook: Regla del dueño sobre los textos de la app
entries.description: Todo texto visible pasa por i18n en es-MX y pt-BR.
entries.body: Ningún string a pelo en las pantallas: todo por `t('...')` con llaves en `locales/es-MX.json` y `locales/pt-BR.json`. Los choferes son de México y Brasil; si falta el portugués no se mergea.

entries.title: Nada de librerías nativas nuevas sin preguntar
entries.hook: Regla del dueño sobre dependencias nativas
entries.description: Una dependencia con código nativo obliga a sacar build a las tiendas; se consulta antes.
entries.body: No metas librerías con código nativo sin preguntarme antes. Cada una obliga a sacar build nuevo a las tiendas y deja a los choferes con la versión vieja hasta que actualicen. Si hay alternativa en JS puro, esa.

entries.title: Offline first for every driver action
entries.hook: Owner rule on how writes behave without network
entries.description: Every driver action must succeed offline and sync later.
entries.body: Anything a driver does (mark delivered, photo, signature, note) must work with no signal and sync later. Never block a screen on a network call.

entries.title: App structure
entries.hook: Where screens, data access and offline sync live
entries.description: expo-router screens in app/, Supabase client in lib/supabase.ts, TanStack Query for reads, the outbox for writes.
entries.body:
- Screens with expo-router in `app/`: `(tabs)/route.tsx`, `(tabs)/history.tsx`, `(tabs)/profile.tsx`, `stop/[id].tsx`.
- Supabase client in `lib/supabase.ts` (session kept in `expo-secure-store`).
- Reads: TanStack Query hooks in `hooks/` (`useRoute`, `useStop`); writes go to the outbox (`lib/outbox.ts`), never straight to Supabase.
- Backend SQL, policies and edge functions live in `supabase/`.

entries.title: OTA updates with expo publish
entries.hook: Publishing a JS-only update to drivers' phones
entries.description: expo publish to the production release channel.
entries.body:
- `expo publish --release-channel production` from a clean main.
- Staging: `--release-channel staging`; builds read their channel from `updates.releaseChannel` in `app.json`.

entries.title: OTA updates with eas update
entries.hook: Publishing, checking and rolling back a JS-only update
entries.description: eas update to the production branch; runtimeVersion follows appVersion, so native changes need a store build.
entries.body:
- Publish: `eas update --branch production --message "fix history crash"` (channel `production` points to branch `production`).
- `runtimeVersion: { policy: "appVersion" }`: phones only take updates built for their app version; any native change (permission, native library) needs `eas build`, not OTA.
- Roll back: `eas update:list --branch production`, then `eas update:republish --group <previous group id>`.
- `expo publish` and release channels are gone.

entries.title: Offline outbox in AsyncStorage
entries.hook: Where offline driver actions are queued
entries.description: Pending writes are a JSON array under the AsyncStorage key @outbox.
entries.body:
- Pending actions are a JSON array under AsyncStorage key `@outbox`, flushed by `flushOutbox()` when NetInfo reports a connection.
- Photos are stored as file:// URIs in the array; the files stay in the cache directory until flushed.

entries.title: Outbox moved to expo-sqlite
entries.hook: How offline actions are stored and synced
entries.description: The offline queue is an expo-sqlite table with per-row retries; AsyncStorage hit Android's size limit.
entries.body:
- Queue is the table `outbox(id, kind, payload_json, attempts, next_attempt_at, created_at)` in `rutas.db` via `expo-sqlite` (`lib/outbox.ts`, schema in `lib/db.ts`).
- `flushOutbox()` runs on NetInfo reconnect and on AppState `active`; failures back off exponentially (max 1h); rows rejected with a 4xx move to `outbox_dead`.
- Why: the AsyncStorage `@outbox` array hit Android's 6 MB limit on long days (`database or disk is full (code 13 SQLITE_FULL)`) and one bad item blocked the rest.
- Photos are copied to `FileSystem.documentDirectory + 'proofs/'`, never left in the cache.

entries.title: Store builds and submission
entries.hook: Shipping a new binary to the App Store and Play Store
entries.description: eas build with the production profile, then eas submit; build numbers auto-increment.
entries.body:
- Bump `version` in `app.config.ts` (build numbers auto-increment: `"autoIncrement": true` in `eas.json`).
- `eas build --profile production --platform all`.
- `eas submit -p ios --latest` (TestFlight) and `eas submit -p android --latest` (track `internal`, promote in Play Console).
- Needed whenever native code, permissions or config plugins change.

entries.title: iOS build fails: profile lacks aps-environment
entries.hook: The iOS build broke after adding push notifications
entries.description: The stored provisioning profile predates the push capability; regenerate it with eas credentials.
entries.body:
Error: `Provisioning profile "*[expo] com.rutas.driver AppStore 2026-04-02T..." doesn't include the aps-environment entitlement.`
- Cause: the push capability was added after the profile was created.
- Fix: `eas credentials -p ios` → production → Provisioning Profile → remove it, then `eas build -p ios --profile production` lets EAS create a new one (needs the Apple account login).

entries.title: expo-doctor: dependencies incompatible with the SDK
entries.hook: Build or dev client fails after installing a package with npm
entries.description: Packages installed with npm install drift from the SDK's versions; npx expo install --fix aligns them.
entries.body:
Message: `Some dependencies are incompatible with the installed expo version: react-native-reanimated@3.6.0 - expected version: ~3.10.1`.
- Always add packages with `npx expo install <pkg>`, not `npm install`.
- Fix: `npx expo install --fix`, then `npx expo-doctor` must report no issues before `eas build`.

entries.title: Row Level Security on driver tables
entries.hook: Why a query returns nothing although the rows exist
entries.description: RLS limits drivers to their own rows; a filtered select returns an empty array, not an error.
entries.body:
- `routes`, `stops` and `proofs` have RLS: a driver sees rows where `driver_id = auth.uid()`; dispatchers pass through `is_dispatcher()`.
- A blocked `select` returns `[]` with no error; check the policy before debugging the query.
- Policies live in `supabase/migrations/*_rls.sql`; test one in SQL with `set local role authenticated; set local request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"<uuid>"}';`.

entries.title: new row violates row-level security policy for table proofs
entries.hook: Saving a delivery proof fails with an RLS error
entries.description: Inserts must set driver_id to the signed-in user, and the Storage path must start with the user's id.
entries.body:
Error: `new row violates row-level security policy for table "proofs"` (code 42501).
- The insert must send `driver_id: session.user.id`; the policy's `with check (driver_id = auth.uid())` rejects anything else.
- The Storage upload has its own policy: the path must be `<user id>/<stop id>.jpg` in bucket `proofs`, otherwise the same error comes from `storage.objects`.

entries.title: Supabase schema changes
entries.hook: Creating a migration, applying it and regenerating the types
entries.description: supabase migration new, db reset locally, db push to the linked project, then regenerate the TypeScript types.
entries.body:
- `supabase migration new add_stop_notes`, then write the SQL in `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_add_stop_notes.sql`.
- Local check: `supabase db reset` (needs Docker running).
- Apply: `supabase db push --linked` (project linked once with `supabase link --project-ref <ref>`).
- Types: `supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/database.types.ts`, and commit the file.

entries.title: Edge function optimize-route
entries.hook: Running and deploying the route optimization function
entries.description: Deno edge function in supabase/functions/optimize-route; serve it locally with an env file, deploy it with the CLI.
entries.body:
- Local: `supabase functions serve optimize-route --env-file supabase/functions/.env.local`.
- Deploy: `supabase functions deploy optimize-route` (JWT verification stays on; the app calls `supabase.functions.invoke('optimize-route', { body })`).
- Secrets: `supabase secrets set ORS_API_KEY=...` (OpenRouteService); `supabase secrets list` to check.

entries.title: Only EXPO_PUBLIC_ variables reach the app
entries.hook: Environment variables that are undefined on the device
entries.description: Expo inlines only EXPO_PUBLIC_* variables into the bundle; others are undefined at runtime, and EAS builds don't read the local .env.
entries.body:
- Use `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`; a plain `SUPABASE_URL` is `undefined` on the device and `createClient` throws `supabaseUrl is required.`
- Restart Metro with `npx expo start -c` after changing `.env`.
- EAS builds don't upload `.env` (it's in `.easignore`): set values with `eas env:create --environment production` or the `env` block in `eas.json`.

entries.title: Unit tests with jest-expo
entries.hook: Running unit tests and mocking Supabase
entries.description: npx jest with the jest-expo preset; Supabase is mocked through __mocks__.
entries.body:
- `npx jest` (preset `jest-expo`); one file: `npx jest lib/outbox.test.ts`.
- Supabase is mocked in `__mocks__/@supabase/supabase-js.ts`; build responses with `mockQuery({ data, error })`.
- expo-sqlite has no native module under jest: the outbox tests use `lib/__tests__/fake-db.ts`.

entries.title: End-to-end tests with Maestro
entries.hook: Running the E2E flows on an emulator or simulator
entries.description: Maestro flows in .maestro/ run against a dev-client build with a seeded test driver.
entries.body:
- Flows in `.maestro/*.yaml`; run one with `maestro test .maestro/deliver-stop.yaml`.
- Needs a dev-client build installed (`eas build --profile e2e -p android` or `npx expo run:android`) and the local Supabase seeded (`supabase db reset` loads `supabase/seed.sql`).
- Test login: driver `e2e-driver` from the seed; its password is in `.maestro/.env` (not committed).

entries.title: deliver-stop E2E flow flaky on the Android emulator
entries.hook: E2E flow that fails now and then at the photo step
entries.description: The camera permission dialog appears late on the emulator; launch the app with permissions already granted.
entries.body:
`.maestro/deliver-stop.yaml` fails ~1 in 5 on the Android emulator with `Element not found: Text matching regex: Take photo`.
- Likely cause: the camera permission dialog shows after the tap and covers the button.
- Fix: `- launchApp: { permissions: { all: allow } }` at the top of the flow instead of tapping "Allow".

entries.title: Background location stops on Android
entries.hook: Driver positions stop updating when the phone is locked
entries.description: Background location needs the background permission, a foreground service and a native build; OTA cannot add it.
entries.body:
Symptom: positions stop ~10 min after the phone locks; logcat shows `Not authorized to use background location services`.
- `app.config.ts`: `android.permissions` must include `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` and `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION`, and the expo-location plugin needs `isAndroidBackgroundLocationEnabled: true`.
- `Location.startLocationUpdatesAsync(LOCATION_TASK, { foregroundService: { notificationTitle: ... } })` in `lib/location-task.ts`.
- Permission changes are native: ship a new `eas build`; an OTA update won't carry them.

entries.title: Unable to resolve module after moving files
entries.hook: Metro can't find a file that was moved or renamed
entries.description: Metro's cache keeps old paths; check the import, then restart with a cleared cache.
entries.body:
Error: `Unable to resolve module ../lib/outbox from app/(tabs)/route.tsx`.
- Check the import first: aliases use `@/lib/...`, configured in `tsconfig.json` and `babel.config.js`.
- Then `npx expo start -c` to clear Metro's cache; on Windows also delete `node_modules/.cache`.

entries.title: Invalid Refresh Token after days in background
entries.hook: Drivers get logged out or see auth errors after the app sat idle
entries.description: Auto refresh doesn't run while the app is backgrounded; start and stop it on AppState, and send users to login on this error.
entries.body:
Error: `AuthApiError: Invalid Refresh Token: Refresh Token Not Found`.
- In `lib/supabase.ts`: `AppState.addEventListener('change', s => s === 'active' ? supabase.auth.startAutoRefresh() : supabase.auth.stopAutoRefresh())`.
- On this error call `supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' })` and route to `/login`, keeping the outbox (it belongs to the device, not the session).

entries.title: Push notifications to drivers
entries.hook: How push tokens are registered and pushes are sent
entries.description: The expo-notifications token is stored on the profile; the notify-driver edge function sends through Expo's push API.
entries.body:
- Token: `Notifications.getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId: Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.eas?.projectId })`; without projectId it throws `No "projectId" found`.
- Saved to `profiles.expo_push_token` on login (`lib/push.ts`).
- Sent by the edge function `notify-driver` via `https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send`; `DeviceNotRegistered` receipts clear the token.
- Push doesn't work on the iOS simulator; use a device with the dev client.

entries.title: Lint, types and file conventions
entries.hook: Checks to run before a PR, and naming conventions
entries.description: npx expo lint and tsc --noEmit; components PascalCase in components/, hooks in hooks/useX.ts.
entries.body:
- `npx expo lint` (eslint-config-expo + prettier) and `npx tsc --noEmit`; both run in CI on every PR.
- Components in `components/` as `PascalCase.tsx`; hooks in `hooks/useThing.ts`; screens compose, they don't fetch inline.
- Imports go through the `@/` alias.

entries.title: Maps: react-native-maps, not Mapbox
entries.hook: Which map library the app uses and why
entries.description: react-native-maps with Google on Android and Apple Maps on iOS; Mapbox was rejected.
entries.body:
- `react-native-maps` (Google provider on Android, Apple Maps on iOS); the route line is a `Polyline` from `optimize-route`'s geometry.
- Rejected `@rnmapbox/maps`: another native SDK, a token to protect, and per-MAU billing for ~300 drivers.
- The Android Google Maps key is `GOOGLE_MAPS_ANDROID_KEY` in EAS env, restricted to the app's SHA-1.

entries.title: Proof-of-delivery photo upload
entries.hook: Compressing and uploading delivery photos to Storage
entries.description: Photos are resized with expo-image-manipulator and uploaded as an ArrayBuffer; supabase-js can't take a file:// URI.
entries.body:
- Resize: `manipulateAsync(uri, [{ resize: { width: 1280 } }], { compress: 0.7, format: SaveFormat.JPEG })`.
- Upload: `supabase.storage.from('proofs').upload(path, arrayBuffer, { contentType: 'image/jpeg', upsert: true })` with `path = driverId + '/' + stopId + '.jpg'`.
- supabase-js on React Native can't upload a `file://` URI or a Blob reliably (the object ends up 0 bytes): read it with `await (await fetch(uri)).arrayBuffer()`.
- Uploads run from the outbox, never directly from the screen.

entries.title: Háblame en español, código en inglés
entries.hook: Idioma de las respuestas
entries.description: Responder en español; código, nombres, comentarios y commits en inglés.
entries.body: Respóndeme siempre en español, aunque a veces te escriba en inglés. El código, los nombres, los comentarios y los commits van en inglés.

entries.description: Lead with the command or the fix, then one line of why; no recaps.
entries.body: Keep answers short: the command or the fix first, then one line of why. No recap of what you did unless I ask. If something wasn't tested, say so in one line.
